config.title: Build LRU cache class

intro.title: Build LRU cache class
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Least Recently Used (LRU) Cache class in JavaScript. An LRU cache is a data structure that stores a limited number of items, automatically removing the least recently used one when full to make space for new entries. You'll learn to implement this using core JavaScript constructs like classes, objects, and arrays to manage the cache's size and access order. This project will help you understand how caching works to optimize data retrieval in applications. By the end, you'll have a functional LRU Cache that can store, retrieve, and efficiently manage key-value pairs.
intro.usecase: An LRU cache is essential in web applications where you need to manage limited memory while keeping frequently accessed data readily available. You'll see this pattern in browser caching systems that store recently visited web pages for faster back/forward navigation, or in e-commerce product listing pages that cache recently viewed items. As a developer, you might implement an LRU cache for an analytics dashboard that caches frequently requested chart data, or for a search component that remembers recent queries to provide instant suggestions. This ensures optimal performance while preventing memory overflow in real-world applications.

objectives: Construct an LRU cache class with a specified capacity limit
Initialize the cache with a Map for storage and a Doubly Linked List for tracking usage order
Implement a get method to retrieve values and update their position as most recently used
Implement a put method to insert key-value pairs while evicting least recently used items when capacity is exceeded
Manipulate the doubly linked list to move nodes to the front on access
Integrate capacity checks to control cache size during insert operations
Apply the LRU eviction policy by removing the tail node when the cache is full

steps.title: Create LRUCache class with constructor
steps.instruction: Create a class named LRUCache with a constructor that accepts a capacity parameter and initializes the cache capacity, a Map for storage, and doubly linked list head/tail references for tracking usage order.
steps.hint: Start with 'class LRUCache {', then define the constructor to set up the initial state of your cache.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a class definition with a constructor that sets up the initial structure for your LRU cache.
successCriteria: The LRUCache class is defined with a constructor that initializes capacity, a Map (or object) for storage, and head/tail properties for the doubly linked list.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your constructor properly initializes all the required properties: capacity, storage (like a Map), and head/tail references for the linked list.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a class named LRUCache with a constructor that sets up the initial state. Remember to initialize the capacity, storage structure, and head/tail properties.

steps.title: Add Node class for doubly linked list
steps.instruction: Inside your LRUCache class, define a Node class with constructor that takes key and value parameters and initializes prev and next properties to null.
steps.hint: Create a nested class inside LRUCache using the class keyword. The constructor should set this.key, this.value, this.prev, and this.next.
steps.expectedOutcome: The LRUCache class will have a nested Node class that can create nodes with key, value, and pointers for the doubly linked list.
successCriteria: Node class is defined inside LRUCache with constructor that sets key, value, prev, and next properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the Node class is defined inside LRUCache and has all four properties: key, value, prev, and next.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Node class needs to be defined inside LRUCache with a constructor that initializes key, value, prev, and next properties.

steps.title: Implement addNode helper method
steps.instruction: Inside the LRUCache class, add a private helper method named addNode that takes a node parameter and inserts it right after the head of the linked list.
steps.hint: Think about how to insert a node in a doubly linked list: you'll need to adjust the next/prev pointers of the new node, the head, and the node currently after the head.
steps.expectedOutcome: The LRUCache class will have an addNode method that correctly inserts a node immediately after the head in the doubly linked list.
successCriteria: The LRUCache class contains an addNode method that properly handles the node insertion by updating all relevant next and prev pointers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an addNode method, but check the pointer assignments. Make sure you're updating both the new node's pointers and the surrounding nodes' pointers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addNode method is missing or doesn't properly insert the node. Remember to adjust the next/prev pointers of the new node, head, and the node currently after head.

steps.title: Implement removeNode helper method
steps.instruction: Inside the LRUCache class, add a helper method called removeNode that takes a node as a parameter and removes it from the doubly linked list by updating its neighbors' pointers.
steps.hint: Update the previous node's next pointer and the next node's previous pointer to bypass the given node.
steps.expectedOutcome: The removeNode method will correctly unlink a node from the doubly linked list by adjusting the pointers of its neighboring nodes.
successCriteria: The LRUCache class contains a removeNode method that updates the previous node's next pointer and the next node's previous pointer to remove the given node.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the removeNode method might not correctly update both neighboring pointers. Make sure to set node.prev.next = node.next and node.next.prev = node.prev.
steps.feedbackWrong: The removeNode method is missing or doesn't properly remove the node. Check that you're updating both the previous and next node pointers to bypass the given node.

steps.title: Implement popTail helper method
steps.instruction: Add a private helper method named popTail to your LRUCache class that removes and returns the node right before the tail (the least recently used item) for eviction.
steps.hint: The popTail method should remove the node before the tail dummy node and return that removed node. This will be used later when the cache is full.
steps.expectedOutcome: The LRUCache class now has a popTail method that can remove and return the least recently used node.
successCriteria: The popTail method is defined inside the LRUCache class and returns the removed node.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your popTail method correctly removes the node before the tail and returns that node.
steps.feedbackWrong: The popTail method is missing or incorrect. It should be a method that removes and returns the node right before the tail.

steps.title: Implement get method
steps.instruction: Add a get method to your LRUCache class that accepts a key parameter, returns the value if the key exists (moving its node to the head), or returns -1 if the key doesn't exist.
steps.hint: Check if the key exists in your cache map. If it does, move that node to the head using moveToHead and return its value. Otherwise, return -1.
steps.expectedOutcome: The LRUCache class will have a get method that correctly retrieves values and updates the usage order.
successCriteria: The get method is added to the class, accepts a key, returns the value if the key exists (moving the node to head), and returns -1 otherwise.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a get method, but check if it properly moves the node to the head when the key exists and returns -1 when it doesn't.
steps.feedbackWrong: The get method is missing or doesn't match the required behavior. Review the instructions and try again.

steps.title: Implement put method for new items
steps.instruction: Inside the LRUCache class, add a put method that takes key and value parameters. In the method body, create a new Node with the given key and value,
steps.hint: The method signature should be put(key, value). Create a new Node instance with the key and value, then use the addNode helper to add it to the head of the list, and store it in the Map.
steps.expectedOutcome: The LRUCache class will have a put method that creates a new node and adds it to the cache when called with a new key-value pair.
successCriteria: The put method is defined with parameters key and value, creates a new Node, adds it to the Map and linked list using the addNode helper.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your put method creates a new Node with the key and value, then adds it to both the Map and the linked list using the addNode helper.
steps.feedbackWrong: The put method isn't implemented correctly. It should take key and value parameters, create a new Node instance, and add it to the Map and linked list.

steps.title: Implement put method for existing items
steps.instruction: Inside the put method, add an else-if branch after the new item logic to handle when the key already exists in the cache: update the node's value and move it to the head.
steps.hint: Check if the key exists in the map, then update the node's value property and call moveToHead with that node.
steps.expectedOutcome: The put method will now correctly update existing cache entries by refreshing their value and moving them to the most-recently-used position.
successCriteria: The put method includes an else-if branch that updates the node's value and calls moveToHead when the key exists in the map.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to update the node's value and call moveToHead within the else-if branch.
steps.feedbackWrong: The put method is missing the logic for existing keys. Add an else-if branch after the new item logic to handle when the key already exists.

steps.title: Implement cache eviction logic in put method
steps.instruction: Complete the put method by adding an else-if branch to handle existing keys: if the key exists in the map, update the node's value and move it to the head.
steps.hint: Inside the else-if branch, get the existing node from the map, update its value property, and call moveToHead with that node.
steps.expectedOutcome: The put method will now correctly handle both new and existing keys, updating existing items and moving them to the most-recently-used position.
successCriteria: The else-if branch updates the value of the existing node and calls moveToHead to mark it as recently used.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your else-if branch updates the node's value property and calls moveToHead with the existing node.
steps.feedbackWrong: The else-if branch is missing or incorrect. Check that you're getting the existing node from the map, updating its value, and calling moveToHead.
